dossier.public_summary: The dips alternate deep and shallow every other transit, and single-transit depths vary from event to event with most signal coming from a few outliers. That matches two different eclipses at ~20 days, not the steady 9.9-day dips expected for a planet. The signal is best explained by a background blended or hierarchical eclipsing binary.

reasons.why: Odd and even transits differ at very high significance and by factor 4.2, classic signature of an eclipsing binary at twice the 9.96 d period with two unequal eclipses, not a planet at this period.
Individual transit depths are highly inconsistent; the signal is driven by a few outliers and not by a consistent planet depth.
Depth changes by >40% between sectors and between odd/even, inconsistent with a planet on a single target; favors a blended or ellipsoidal binary where dilution and eclipse depth vary.
